work.problem: Journal two findings from 2026-11-17 through capa issues and the projector: (A) #55's WIF attribute_condition left its subject alternatives unbracketed, so the owner-ID and repository pins covered only the PR plan subject from 11:05 to 11:56 CT (fixed by sovereign #64); (B) the hand-applied identity unit was planned three times from code other than intended (a stale checkout, then main before #64), caught only by comparing counts (KAN-113).

findings.reason: Same unit and the same root: the identity unit is applied by hand and never planned in CI, so nothing reads what it renders. F-0097 found that #38's change was never applied; here #55's rendered condition was never checked. Both new findings cite it as a cause; neither is a recurrence, since F-0097 is open and its fingerprint differs.

Its lesson (check platform behaviour in the docs, not from memory) applies to the root cause sentence 'CEL binds && tighter than ||'. Checked before writing: CEL's operator table lists conditional AND above conditional OR (cel-spec langdef; Firebase's CEL reference). The checker's tests also refuse the live string, so the claim is tested, not only cited.

A check counts only once shown to fail on its defect. The preventive check (check_wif_condition.py) was: the live condition string is refused, the module-source test fails on the pre-#64 main, and the owner's run on the real plan printed PASS on the fix.

Merged without its real path running: #55's condition merged green because no CI path renders the identity unit. The same shape (a merge proves nothing about a path that did not run) is the root cause stated in finding A.

Diagnosed from the code, not the live state. This time the diagnosis came from the live state: the owner's apply output, at 11:05 CT, showed the rendered condition. The entries cite that output, not the module source alone.
The apply workflow is disabled, so the fix cannot be verified for the apply subject with a real token. The verification states this instead of claiming all three subjects were proven.

The defect arrived with the KAN-67 elastic-pool work that answers F-0034, F-0084 and F-0091. The pool's scale-to-zero now runs (scaler logs 17:47-17:57Z, 2026-11-17), but those findings close in their own change, not in this journal PR.
As F-0034: same KAN-67 work; its closure needs the designed-to-fail alert run, not done here.
As F-0034: the scaler never shrinks below busy VMs, which answers F-0091; its closure is a separate change.

A sibling identity finding in the same module: #61 (its fix) also changes modules/identity/main.tf. After #64, #61 was merged with main and still brackets the condition; its next identity apply runs the same check.
The defect was agent-authored, and Git cannot tell the agent's commits from the owner's until KAN-69. The entry says 'agent-authored' from the PR body's statement, not from Git authorship.
This branch keeps the clone's configured author; no identity is set on the command line.

Branch protection: #55 merged with a human review, and the review missed the precedence. The preventive action is a check, not more review, consistent with F-0038's lesson that a control must run rather than be relied on.
The design record's gate; #55 had a design record (docs/design/2026-11-16-elastic-plan-pool.md), and the defect is in the rendered IAM condition, not the record.
The failing apply's history; context for F-0085 only. It changes nothing in these entries.
Runner boot time; the baked image from #55 is unaffected by the condition.
The Python gate path on the Debian pool; not involved.
An agent ran a download the owner had stopped. No download or stopped action is involved here; listed for completeness of the agent-conduct findings.

lessons: Severity comes from the register's written rubric, not from a first guess: a control that admits what it must refuse is critical, even when fixed within the hour.
A hand-applied unit needs a machine check on its rendered plan, because CI never renders it (F-0097, F-0092).
State what the verification proved per subject; the apply subject cannot be proven while apply is disabled (F-0085).
Platform semantics in a root cause are checked in the docs first (F-0094).
uncertainty: Whether any token was accepted on sub alone from outside the owner's repository between 11:05 and 11:56 CT was not checked: STS audit logs were not read from this session. Exploiting it needed the Drecoder/sovereign-vpc-gcp name held by another account.
KAN-113's preventive guard is designed, not built; finding B stays open.
